question: Which filesystem policy contract should OpenClaw support for host-mode agents, and should the first version include exec-mediated filesystem access or explicitly split exec into a separate boundary?
rationale: Current main only has `tools.fs.workspaceOnly`, while open PRs propose incompatible public config surfaces and leave different parts of the filesystem boundary out of scope.

options.title: Land file-tool policy first
options.body: Choose a `tools.fs` roots or allow/deny contract for file/media/apply_patch tools, document that exec remains outside v1, and keep a separate exec-boundary issue open.

options.title: Require unified RWX policy
options.body: Pause file-tool-only PRs until maintainers design one policy model spanning read/write/edit/apply_patch and shell-mediated filesystem effects.

options.title: Stay with current hardening
options.body: Decline granular host path policy for now and recommend Docker/OS-user isolation plus `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` for supported hardening.

recommendation.title: Land file-tool policy first
recommendation.body: Choose a `tools.fs` roots or allow/deny contract for file/media/apply_patch tools, document that exec remains outside v1, and keep a separate exec-boundary issue open.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the shipped workspace-only guard and has the clearest prior review signal on this exact security/config boundary.
